Scheduler accounts both softirq and interrupt processing times to the
currently running task. This means
for some other task in the system
column2: then the current task ends up being

column1: penalized as it gets shorter runtime than otherwise.
Change sched task accounting to acoount only actual task time from
currently running task. Now update_curr()
depend on rq->clock_task.
Note that this change only handles CONFIG_IRQ_TIME_ACCOUNTING case. We can
extend this to CONFIG_VIRT_CPU_ACCOUNTING with minimal effort. But
for later.
This change will impact scheduling behavior in interrupt heavy conditions.
Tested on a 4-way system with eth0 handled by CPU 2 and a network heavy
task (nc) running on CPU 3 (and no RSS/RFS). With that I have CPU 2
spending 75%+ of its time in irq processing. CPU 3 spending around 35%
time running nc task.
Now
column2: if I run another CPU intensive task on CPU 2

column1: /proc/<pid>/schedstat shows 100% of time accounted to this task. With this
change
column2: it rightly shows less than 25% accounted to this task as remaining

column1: time is actually spent on irq processing.
